task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req177-dlq-hooks.md or similar) for REQ-177: wire two DLQ landing call sites, deliberately narrow (landing only, not re-execution). (1) SERVICE_TASK retry-exhaustion: find/design the correct call site where a future orchestrator (or, if no such orchestrator exists yet in this codebase, specify precisely where THIS requirement itself must add the call -- do not assume an orchestrator exists without verifying) observes ServiceTask.decide_failure/3 returning :give_up due to attempt_index >= retry_limit specifically (not an immediately-non-retriable failure -- the requirement's own acceptance criteria specifically require 'attempt_index == retry_limit', i.e. genuine exhaustion, not day-one non-retriability -- design must distinguish these two :give_up causes if decide_failure/3's return value doesn't already), and calls Letflow.Dlq.enqueue/2 with entry_type "event", instance_id set, full_reason naming the classified failure kind, source_payload carrying the attempted request. (2) Instance ERROR landing: extend Letflow.Engine.ExecutionError.append_multi/3's Multi chain (or engine.ex's set_instance_error/2 wrapper, whichever is the more correct integration point per the existing Multi-composition discipline) with an ADDITIONAL Multi step that calls Letflow.Dlq.enqueue/2 (or an internal insert matching its exact behavior) IN THE SAME transaction as the status flip and EXECUTION_ERROR event append -- full_reason must be read back from the just-persisted EXECUTION_ERROR event's own reason field (query it back, do not pass the caller's original reason string forward, per this project's re-derive-from-source discipline already cited in the requirement text). Design must explicitly resolve REQ-176's two open questions this now-building requirement was told to decide: whether last_failed_at should be set on landing, and confirm exhaustion-driven-landing's exact trigger condition. Design must specify the moduledoc language for BOTH hook sites naming retry/2's no-op-beyond-the-DLQ-entry behavior as a deliberately deferred follow-up (naming what's missing: a wired SERVICE_TASK transport, an operator-driven ERROR-recovery path). Design only -- no implementation code -- and no fenced code block reproducing real .ex content (this project's mechanical, no-exceptions rule, caught real defects on REQ-157/174/176 in this exact pipeline).
acceptance_criteria: a SERVICE_TASK dispatch driven to retry-exhaustion (attempt_index == retry_limit) produces exactly one dlq_entries row via enqueue/1, with entry_type "event", instance_id set, and full_reason naming the classified failure kind -- read back from the database, not asserted from the caller's own return value

an instance driven to ERROR via REQ-061's execution-error path produces exactly one dlq_entries row via enqueue/1, with entry_type "event", instance_id set, and full_reason equal to the persisted EXECUTION_ERROR event's own reason field

the ERROR-path DLQ landing is in the same transaction as REQ-061's status flip and event append: forcing the DLQ insert to fail leaves the instance status, the EXECUTION_ERROR event, and the DLQ table all unchanged, verified by reading all three back

a test explicitly asserts that calling REQ-176's retry/2 against one of these two entries transitions the DLQ entry to "retrying" but does NOT re-invoke the original SERVICE_TASK dispatch and does NOT change the instance's own status away from ERROR -- naming both non-effects, not just the one effect that does happen

the moduledoc for both hook sites names REQ-176's retry/2 no-op-beyond-the-DLQ-entry behavior as a deferred follow-up (naming what would need to exist for it to do more: a wired SERVICE_TASK transport, an operator-driven ERROR-recovery path) rather than leaving it unremarked
no file outside the two named hook call sites and their tests is modified, confirmed by git diff --stat
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
